title: Look around
briefing: Your home directory is not empty.
tips: To see what's in a directory, list it. The command is two letters.
Once you know a file's name, print it: cat NAME
objective: Find the file waiting in your home directory and read it. It contains a codeword.
expert_objective: There is a codeword somewhere in your home directory. Retrieve it.
hints: First find out what's there. The command that lists files is very short.
`ls` lists files. To print a file's content use `cat` (from 'concatenate') followed by the file name.

reactions.say: There's a file. Now print what's inside it — and you can press Tab to complete its name.

explanation: `ls` lists a directory; `cat` prints a file. Linux keeps nearly all configuration in plain text, so reading files is half of system administration. Tab-completion saves typing and typos. And did you read the P.S.?
